LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2018, 2020, 2023) and earned numerous accolades, including four NBA Most Valuable Player awards, 17 All‑NBA selections, and 18 NBA All‑Star appearances. His playing style—combining size, athleticism, court vision, and scoring ability—has made him a dominant force on both ends of the floor.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron to support at‑risk children. He is also a media entrepreneur, co‑founding the production company SpringHill Entertainment and launching the streaming platform Uninterrupted. In addition, he has been involved in various business ventures, endorsements, and political activism, using his platform to advocate for social justice and community empowerment.
